title: SKOG Haus Coffee & Tea
venue_description:
SKOG Haus Coffee & Tea

SKOG Haus Coffee & Tea is a family-owned neighborhood cafe in Mountlake Terrace just north of Seattle. Heather and Dave Skogerson started SKOG as a mobile coffee trailer and opened the brick-and-mortar shop in 2024. The cafe pours coffee and tea from small Pacific Northwest roasters and makes a point of sourcing ingredients from other local small businesses.

Sunday Open Mic and Featured Artist

Most Sundays from 3:00 PM to 5:00 PM SKOG Haus hosts a free all-ages open mic where artists of every experience level are welcome. On the final Sunday of each month the open mic gives way to a featured local artist who plays an extended set. Music is the main focus but poetry is welcome too and the whole event is family friendly.

Atmosphere and Setting

This is a daytime coffeehouse stage with a relaxed and supportive crowd. It is a great fit for acoustic players and singer-songwriters and anyone trying out new material for the first time. Families and neighbors drop in for a latte and stay for a few songs.

Food and Drink

SKOG serves espresso drinks and loose-leaf teas along with pastries and light bites. The cafe is committed to sustainability and nearly everything it serves in is compostable.

Good to Know

SKOG Haus is at 24015 Van Ry Boulevard Suite 200 in Mountlake Terrace Washington 98043. The open mic is free and all ages. Visit skoghauscoffee.com or follow SKOG Haus Coffee on Facebook for featured artist announcements.
location: 24015 Van Ry Blvd Suite 200, Mountlake Terrace, WA 98043

title: Little Red Hen
venue_description:
Little Red Hen

The Little Red Hen is Seattle's oldest country music venue and one of the city's most beloved dive bars. The business dates to 1933 and it has called its Green Lake location on Woodlawn Avenue home since 1968. It is one of the only places in Seattle where you can walk in any night of the week and hear a live band or join a packed dance floor.

History and Community

The Hen has been through a long lease dispute with its landlord since 2025. The bar stayed open throughout the legal fight and the Save The Hen campaign gathered more than 7000 petition signatures from fans who want to keep this nearly century-old honky tonk alive. Owner Dominic Shim and the staff have kept the music going seven nights a week.

Weekly Music Schedule

  • Sundays: Open Mic Jam at 7:00 PM hosted by Billy Bodacious
  • Mondays: Line Dance Party
  • Tuesdays: Bluegrass Jam from 7:00 PM with host Stan Hall
  • Wednesdays: Karaoke Night
  • Thursdays through Saturdays: Live country and roots bands

Sunday Open Mic Jam

Sunday evenings belong to local players. Billy Bodacious hosts the Open Mic Jam and surprise special guests often sit in. Expect country and blues and rock and roots music with a friendly crowd that likes to dance.

Tuesday Bluegrass Jam

The Tuesday jam is organized with the Outlanders Progressive Bluegrass Social Club. Beginners gather for an informal picking circle around 7:00 PM and the stage set with more polished players starts around 8:15 PM. Bring a banjo or fiddle or mandolin or guitar and join in.

Atmosphere

Wood paneling and neon and a well-worn dance floor give the Hen its classic honky tonk feel. Two-steppers and line dancers share the room with bluegrass pickers and neighborhood regulars. Happy hour runs daily from 3:00 PM to 6:00 PM.

Good to Know

The Little Red Hen is at 7115 Woodlawn Avenue NE in Seattle 98115 near Green Lake. It is 21 and over. Hours are Sunday through Tuesday 3:00 PM to midnight and Wednesday and Thursday 3:00 PM to 1:30 AM and Friday and Saturday 3:00 PM to 2:00 AM. Call (206) 522-1168 and check littleredhenseattle.com for the latest schedule.

title: Orient Express
venue_description:
Orient Express

Orient Express is one of Seattle's most unusual nightspots. The SoDo restaurant and lounge is built inside eight vintage railroad cars and each car has its own story. It is best known for its private karaoke rooms but it also books concerts and special music nights.

Music and Entertainment

Eight private karaoke rooms hold anywhere from 10 to 45 people and the main bar space can host up to 300 guests. The lounge has hosted rock and metal and punk shows and it is presenting an Open Mic Jazz Night where singers can step up and perform their favorite jazz standards with live musicians.

Food and Drink

The kitchen serves Thai and Chinese dishes and there is a full bar. Happy hour starts at 3:00 PM daily and the bar and karaoke rooms stay open until 2:00 AM.

Atmosphere

The train car setting makes every night feel like a party. It is a fun stop before or after a game in the nearby stadium district.

Good to Know

Orient Express is at 2963 Fourth Avenue South in Seattle 98134. Music events are 21 and over. Call (206) 682-0683 or visit orientexpresslounge.com.

title: Conor Byrne Pub
venue_description:
Conor Byrne Pub

Conor Byrne Pub is a Ballard institution with more than a century of musical history. The building on historic Ballard Avenue once housed The Owl Saloon and today it is one of Seattle's most important small rooms for folk and Americana and roots and indie music.

A Community-Owned Venue

In May 2024 the community stepped in to save Conor Byrne by turning it into a cooperative. The co-op now has more than 600 member-owners and it is fiscally sponsored by Shunpike Arts. Membership is open to anyone who wants to help keep live music alive in Ballard.

Sunday Open Mic

The Conor Byrne Open Mic runs every Sunday and many call it the best open mic in Seattle. Sign-ups are at 7:30 PM sharp and the music runs until 1:00 AM. The room is full of songwriters and folk players and bands trying new material and the audience is known for listening.

More Music and Events

The calendar includes touring and local bands most nights along with Country Dancing nights and free two-step and Lindy Hop lessons. Matinee shows and happy hour music trivia and bingo round out the week.

Atmosphere

Dark wood and a long bar and a small stage give Conor Byrne the feel of a classic Irish pub with a serious music program. Seating is first come first served.

Good to Know

Conor Byrne is at 5140 Ballard Avenue NW in Seattle 98107. It is 21 and over. Hours are Sunday from noon to 2:00 AM and Monday through Saturday from 5:00 PM to 2:00 AM. Parking is on the street. Call (206) 784-3640 or visit conorbyrnepub.com.

title: Darrell's Tavern
venue_description:
Darrell's Tavern

Darrell's Tavern is a popular dive bar and live music room on Aurora Avenue in Shoreline just north of Seattle. Carpet-covered walls and vintage lighting give it a proudly retro look and the drinks are cheap. It is one of the hardest working small stages in the north end.

Live Music Every Weekend

Darrell's books local and touring bands of every flavor including rock and punk and country and metal and soul and jazz and funk and ska. Thursday through Saturday nights usually feature three or four band bills and the room also hosts special nights like Opera on Tap and the Shoreline Music Fest.

Wednesday Open Mic

Darrell's venerable open mic runs every Wednesday at 7:30 PM. It is free and it welcomes singer-songwriters and bands and anyone with something to share.

Sunday Jazz Jam

Every Sunday night at 7:00 PM Darrell's hosts a Jazz Jam led by Kevin McCarthy. There is a $10 suggested donation and jazz players are welcome to sit in.

Atmosphere

This is an unpretentious neighborhood bar where musicians outnumber the pretense. Expect a friendly crowd and a loud and loving support system for local music.

Good to Know

Darrell's Tavern is at 18041 Aurora Avenue North in Shoreline Washington 98133. It is 21 and over. For booking email jjbooksyourband@gmail.com and check the Darrell's show calendar.

title: Slim's Last Chance
venue_description:
Slim's Last Chance

Slim's Last Chance is a chili shack and watering hole in Georgetown that doubles as one of South Seattle's favorite roots and rock venues. It is known for big bowls of chili and a roomy stage that hosts rockabilly and country and punk and blues.

Monday Open Mic with Levi said.

Every Monday from 6:00 PM to 9:00 PM Levi said. hosts an open mic at Slim's. Music and spoken word and even puppets are all welcome. Arrive at 5:30 PM to sign up. There is no cover.

Live Music

The weekend calendar brings local and touring bands with a focus on roots rock and country and garage and blues. Sunday shows happen on show days only.

Food and Drink

Chili is the star of the menu with plenty of toppings and sides. The kitchen runs from 11:00 AM to 8:00 PM and the bar serves beer and cocktails.

Good to Know

Slim's Last Chance is at 5606 First Avenue South in Georgetown Seattle 98108. Shows are 21 and over. Hours are Monday through Thursday 11:00 AM to 10:00 PM and Friday and Saturday 11:00 AM to 1:00 AM and Sunday 11:00 AM to 10:00 PM on show days. Call (206) 762-7900 or visit slimslastchance.com.

title: Cottontail
venue_description:
Cottontail

Cottontail is a cozy cocktail bar and speakeasy with an alley entrance in Belltown. It occupies part of the 1924 building that once housed Sit & Spin which was an influential Seattle music venue and laundromat in the 1990s and 2000s. Owner Jessica Gifford also runs Bathtub Gin & Co. and Lava Lounge and Rabbit Hole.

Belltown Open Mic

Every Tuesday from 7:00 PM to 10:30 PM Cottontail hosts the Belltown Open Mic. It is a fun night to showcase or listen to music and other performance art in an intimate speakeasy. Sign-ups are first come first served and there is an in-house piano for performers.

Atmosphere

Low light and local art on the walls and a rotating cocktail menu make Cottontail a great hideaway. The bar is dog friendly and 21 and over.

Next Door at Luka's

The front of the same building is home to Luka's Sit Sip & Roll which hosts the Thursday Sunset Series Showcase and DJs on weekends.

Good to Know

Cottontail is at 2219 Fourth Avenue in Belltown Seattle 98121 with the entrance in the alley. It is open daily from 4:00 PM to 2:00 AM. Visit cottontailclubseattle.com or follow @cottontail_club on Instagram.

title: The Mountain Room: Bar at the R
venue_description:
The Mountain Room: Bar at the R

The Mountain Room is a bar and live music venue inside Seattle's historic Old Rainier Brewery on Airport Way. The landmark brick complex with its famous red R sign is now home to artists and makers and The Mountain Room has become its social hub.

Tuesday Open Mic

Every Tuesday The Mountain Room hosts Open Mic Night. Sign-up starts at 7:00 PM and music starts at 7:30 PM. Tuesday is also an all-day happy hour so it is an easy night to come out and support local players.

Live Music and Karaoke

The calendar mixes ticketed shows that range from psychedelic soul to post-punk and industrial with Karaoke Under The R nights and art walk events.

Atmosphere

The room has an industrial brewery setting with a relaxed neighborhood bar feel. Happy hour runs from 4:00 PM to 7:00 PM on weekdays and all day on Tuesdays and Wednesdays.

Good to Know

The Mountain Room is at 3100 Airport Way South in Building 3 of the Old Rainier Brewery in Seattle. It is 21 and over with valid ID. Visit themountainroomseattle.com or follow @mountainroom.seattle on Instagram.
location: 3100 Airport Way S Building 3, Seattle, WA 98134

title: Tim's Tavern
venue_description:
Tim's Tavern

Tim's Tavern is a neighborhood music venue and kitchen and gathering space in the heart of White Center. Its stage hosts indie and folk and punk and hip-hop and jazz and more and it has become one of the most welcoming rooms in South King County.

Tuesday Open Mic with Levi said.

Every Tuesday Levi said. hosts the Tim's Open Mic. Songs and stories and poetry and puppets and first drafts are all welcome. Sign-ups start at 6:30 PM and slots begin at 7:00 PM with 15 minutes each. There is no cover and performers get food specials.

Mode Music All-Ages Open Mic

On select Wednesdays at 6:00 PM Mode Music and Performing Arts hosts an all-ages open mic that gives young musicians a real stage to play on.

Atmosphere

Tim's is kid friendly until 10:00 PM and it has a dog-friendly patio. The crowd is local and supportive and the room feels like a community living room.

Good to Know

Tim's Tavern is at 9655 16th Avenue SW in White Center Seattle 98106. Hours are Monday through Thursday 4:00 PM to 10:30 PM and Friday and Saturday noon to midnight and Sunday noon to 10:00 PM. Call (206) 588-2452 or visit timslivemusic.com.

title: The Kraken Bar & Lounge
venue_description:
The Kraken Bar & Lounge

The Kraken Bar & Lounge is a punk rock dive bar in Seattle's Roosevelt neighborhood near the University District. It serves food and drinks and live music with plenty of attitude and it is one of the north end's most loved late-night hangouts.

Tuesday Open Mic

Every Tuesday the Kraken hosts an open mic. Sign-up is at 7:30 PM and the show starts at 8:00 PM. Rockers and songwriters and experimental acts all find a spot on the list.

Live Music

The Kraken books punk and garage and metal and indie bands along with karaoke nights. It is a true grassroots room where new bands cut their teeth.

Atmosphere

Expect dim lights and loud music and a friendly crew of regulars. The kitchen stays open until close.

Good to Know

The Kraken is at 5828 Roosevelt Way NE in Seattle 98105. It is 21 and over and open daily from 3:00 PM to 1:00 AM. Call (206) 385-9609 or follow The Kraken on Facebook.

title: Chop Suey
venue_description:
Chop Suey

Chop Suey is a Capitol Hill music club with high ceilings and a dark and loose vibe. For more than two decades it has been a home for indie rock and punk and hip-hop and electronic music and dance nights from Seattle's underground.

Scrambler Jam

Scrambler Jam is part open mic and part open jam session with comics in supporting roles. It runs on the fourth Tuesday of the month. Sign-ups start at 7:00 PM and the show starts at 8:00 PM. A full backline is provided and admission is free. Organizers say the audience is just as important as the performers.

Live Music

The calendar is packed with local and touring bands and dance parties. Chop Suey is a key stop for up-and-coming artists and a favorite room for Seattle bands.

Food and Drink

The bar pours beer and cocktails and the venue has served burgers and bar food from its kitchen.

Good to Know

Chop Suey is at 1325 East Madison Street on Capitol Hill in Seattle 98122. Scrambler Jam is 21 and over. Email info@chopsuey.com or booking@chopsuey.com and see the Chop Suey calendar.

title: Historic Issaquah Train Depot
venue_description:
Historic Issaquah Train Depot

The Historic Issaquah Train Depot is a restored railroad depot in downtown Issaquah that is operated by Issaquah History Museums. The depot museum tells the story of the railroad in the Issaquah Valley and it is also the home base for the Issaquah Valley Trolley.

Historically Hip Open Mic

On the first Wednesday of each month the depot hosts the Historically Hip Open Mic. Performers sign in at 6:00 PM and the show runs live from 6:30 PM to 9:00 PM. It is free and all ages and it welcomes musicians and poets and storytellers.

More Events

The depot also hosts trolley rides and literary nights and holiday caroling and other community events. Downtown Issaquah hosts additional open mics through the year including an alfresco open mic at the historic Shell station.

Atmosphere

A small historic building with a warm small-town crowd. Acoustic acts sound wonderful here and families are welcome.

Good to Know

The depot is at 78 First Avenue NE in Issaquah Washington 98027. Call Issaquah History Museums at (425) 392-3500 or visit issaquahhistorymuseums.com and Downtown Issaquah events.

title: Couth Buzzard Books
venue_description:
Couth Buzzard Books

Couth Buzzard Books is a used bookstore and cafe in Greenwood that has served the neighborhood for more than three decades. It is part bookshop and part coffeehouse and part community center and its community space hosts music and poetry and discussion groups almost every day of the week.

Wednesday Open Mic

The all-acoustic Open Mic runs every Wednesday from 6:45 PM to 9:00 PM. It is one of the most friendly and eclectic open mics in Seattle and it is hosted by musician and award-winning author Chuck Gould. Music and poetry and dance and any creative expression are encouraged.

Songwriters in Seattle Showcase

On the first Saturday of the month from 7:00 PM to 9:00 PM the Songwriters in Seattle showcase presents sets by four or five local songwriters hosted by Roo & the Few.

Irish Music Jam

On the first and third Saturdays at noon traditional players gather for the Irish Music Jam. Bring an instrument and join the session or just come to listen.

More Music

Couth Buzzard books one-off performances on Friday and Saturday evenings from 7:00 PM to 9:00 PM along with other participatory music groups. Musicians can apply through the booking form on the website.

Food and Drink

The cafe serves coffee and wine and sandwiches so you can browse the shelves before the music starts.

Good to Know

Couth Buzzard is at 8310 Greenwood Avenue North in Seattle 98103. Hours are Monday 10:00 AM to 7:00 PM and Wednesday through Friday 10:00 AM to 9:00 PM and Saturday 9:00 AM to 9:00 PM and Sunday 9:00 AM to 7:00 PM. It is closed Tuesdays. Call (206) 436-2960 or see the Couth Buzzard event calendar.

title: Blue Moon Tavern
venue_description:
Blue Moon Tavern

The Blue Moon Tavern is one of Seattle's most storied dive bars. Hank Reverman opened it in 1934 just after Prohibition ended and it became a hangout for University of Washington writers and poets including Theodore Roethke and Richard Hugo. Activists saved the building from demolition around 1990 and the Blue Moon celebrated its 90th anniversary in 2024.

Wednesday Open Mic

Jonny and Odin host one of Seattle's oldest open mics every Wednesday and it has been running for around 30 years. Sign-up is at 7:30 PM and the first act goes on at 8:00 PM. A full house drum kit and bass rig are provided and all performers are welcome. Heavy metal and jazz and blues harmonica and poetry have all shared the same night.

Weekly Music

  • Sundays: Art and Crafts Night followed by Karaoke
  • Mondays: Andy Coe Band at 9:00 PM
  • Tuesdays: DJs in a Dive Bar at 7:00 PM
  • Wednesdays: Open Mic
  • Weekends: Local band bills and psychedelic and rock shows

Atmosphere

Yellowed photos and local art cover the walls and the booths are full of history. It is one of the last bars where you can sit by yourself and talk and the crowd is famously open to unconventional performances.

Good to Know

The Blue Moon is at 712 NE 45th Street in the University District Seattle 98105. It is 21 and over. Hours are Monday through Saturday 3:00 PM to 2:00 AM and Sunday 3:00 PM to midnight. Happy hour is 3:00 PM to 6:00 PM daily. Call (206) 675-9116 or visit thebluemoonseattle.com.

title: Mr. B's Mead Center
venue_description:
Mr. B's Mead Center

Mr. B's Mead Center is a mead tasting room and all-ages community venue in South Delridge. It describes itself as a venue made for artists by artists and it charges no event fees to artists who want to host an event or class.

Mr. B's Open Mic Night

On the fourth Wednesday of each month Mr. B hosts an open mic for musicians and poets and writers and performers with other special skills. Sign-ups start at 6:30 PM and the open mic runs from 7:00 PM until close. It is free and all ages and mead is $2 off all night.

More Events

The calendar includes monthly art walks and quarterly pop-up markets with no vendor fees and live music and weekly Rock Band gaming nights along with comedy and story hours.

Food and Drink

Mr. B's pours its own mead along with wine and beer and sells bottles to go.

Good to Know

Mr. B's Mead Center is at 9444 Delridge Way SW in Seattle 98106 and there is free parking. Call (206) 355-4067 or visit mrbsmeadery.com.

title: Hopvine Pub
venue_description:
Hopvine Pub

Hopvine Pub is one of the only post-Prohibition taverns on Capitol Hill with roots going back to 1933. It was fully renovated in 1995 and it remains a cozy neighborhood pub on 15th Avenue East with local craft beer and hand-tossed pizza.

Wednesday Open Mic

For more than 25 years Hopvine has hosted the longest-running open mic on Capitol Hill. It runs every Wednesday from 8:00 PM to 11:00 PM. Sign-up is from 7:00 PM to 7:45 PM and a lottery at 7:45 PM sets the order for 15 performers. There is no cover but a purchase is required.

More Weekly Events

  • Mondays: ASL Social Hour from 5:30 PM to 7:30 PM
  • Tuesdays and Thursdays: Head in the Clouds Trivia at 7:30 PM
  • Saturdays: Karaoke and live music from 8:00 PM to 1:00 AM

Food and Drink

The menu features pizza and smoked-meat sandwiches and salads and soups with gluten-free and vegetarian options. The taps rotate local craft beers.

Good to Know

Hopvine is at 507 15th Avenue East on Capitol Hill in Seattle 98112. It is open daily from 1:00 PM to midnight and the open mic is 21 and over. Call (206) 328-3120 or visit hopvinepub.com.

title: Swamp Cow Kava Lounge
venue_description:
Swamp Cow Kava Lounge

Swamp Cow Kava Lounge is an alcohol-free kava bar two blocks from Climate Pledge Arena and the Space Needle. It bills itself as a space for authentic connection and it has a sound system and a modest stage for local performers.

Thursday Open Mic

Every Thursday from 7:00 PM to 10:00 PM Swamp Cow hosts Open Mic at The Swamp. Sign-ups start at 6:30 PM and sets are 10 minutes or 2 songs. Kerry Courtney hosts and the night welcomes sound and vocal artists of every skill level.

More Weekly Events

  • Wednesdays: Trivia Night from 7:30 PM
  • Fridays: Live music with Kerry Courtney and Friday Night Live shows
  • Fridays and Sundays: Last Bula game nights

Atmosphere

This is a sober-friendly and relaxed room with comfy seating and WiFi. It is a great option for performers and fans who want live music without alcohol. Open mic is 18 and over.

Good to Know

Swamp Cow is at 159 Denny Way Suite 105 in Seattle 98109. Hours are Wednesday through Sunday 4:00 PM to 11:00 PM and it is closed Monday and Tuesday. Call (206) 845-3758 or visit swampcowkavalounge.com.

title: Luka's Sit Sip & Roll
venue_description:
Luka's Sit Sip & Roll

Luka's Sit Sip & Roll is a flexible bar and event space in Belltown that occupies the historic former home of The Sit & Spin music venue. It shares a building with the Cottontail speakeasy and offers a warm and eclectic room with plenty of open space.

Sunset Series Showcase

Every Thursday from 8:00 PM to 10:15 PM Luka's hosts the Sunset Series Showcase with spoken word and live music and other art forms. The show is free.

More Music

Rotating DJs spin every Friday and Saturday and Luka's also hosts live music and monthly wine tastings and private parties. The Infatuation described the vibe as calm crowds and fun cocktails with live music that can fade into the background or be the main event.

Atmosphere

Games and comfy seating and a good cocktail list make Luka's an easy place to spend an evening.

Good to Know

Luka's is at 2219 Fourth Avenue in Belltown Seattle 98121. It is 21 and over. Email jessica@jmbelltown.com or follow @lukasbelltown on Instagram and visit lukasseattle.com.

title: The Whit's End
venue_description:
The Whit's End

The Whit's End is a cozy and casual neighborhood bar on Phinney Ridge. It has pool and steel-tip darts and pinball and a jukebox and it hosts karaoke and trivia along with a popular open mic.

Open Mic

The Whit's End Open Mic runs on the second and fourth Thursdays of the month from 8:00 PM to midnight with sign-up at 7:30 PM. Play solo or form a jam on the spot. Drums and keys and bass are available.

More Events

Trivia runs weekly on Tuesdays and karaoke nights fill out the calendar. The bar also opens early for Chicago Bears and Tottenham Hotspur and Oregon Ducks games.

Food and Drink

There are 11 beers on tap along with spirits and wine by the glass. The kitchen serves sliders and mac and cheese and tri-tip and tots.

Good to Know

The Whit's End is at 6510 Phinney Avenue North in Seattle 98103. It is 21 and over and open daily from about noon to 2:00 AM. Call (206) 850-8888 or visit thewhitsendbar.com.

title: C&P Coffee Company
venue_description:
C&P Coffee Company

C&P Coffee Company is a beloved West Seattle coffeehouse set in a vintage house on California Avenue. It is a neighborhood living room with a cozy music space and a long history of supporting local songwriters.

Songwriter Showcase

On the second Friday of each month from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM C&P hosts the Songwriter Showcase presented by Songwriters In Seattle. Four local songwriters each play a 25-minute set of original songs. Todd Christoffel hosts and performers sign up in advance through the Songwriters In Seattle group.

Atmosphere

This is a true listening room where original songs get the attention they deserve. The crowd is local and warm and all ages are welcome.

Food and Drink

C&P serves coffee and espresso drinks along with pastries and snacks. There is an ADA ramp and a handicapped parking spot in the back lot.

Good to Know

C&P is at 5612 California Avenue SW in West Seattle 98136. Hours are Monday through Thursday 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM and Friday 6:00 AM to 8:00 PM and Saturday 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM and Sunday 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM. Call (206) 933-3125 or visit candpcoffee.com.

title: Kenyon Hall
venue_description:
Kenyon Hall

Kenyon Hall is a historic nonprofit performance hall in West Seattle. It was built more than a century ago as the Olympic Heights Social Hall and it is owned by the Seattle Artists organization. Its signature feature is a Mighty Wurlitzer theater organ.

A Venue Run by Artists

Longtime operator Lou Magor kept the hall alive for decades. After his passing volunteers Murphy Janssen and Nick Shadel stepped up to co-direct the hall. They describe it as artist-focused and not profit-focused and they offer performers free demo recordings and mentoring.

Monthly Open Mic

Singer-songwriters are welcome on the third Friday of every month. Doors and sign-up are at 6:00 PM and performances start at 6:30 PM. The open mic is presented with The El and it is free and all ages and seated.

More Music

Kenyon Hall presents classical ensembles and contemporary musicians and cabaret nights along with Pocket Sessions instrumental jams and free jazz jams. The Improv Kerfuffle and the West Seattle Story Slam add comedy and storytelling to the mix.

Good to Know

Kenyon Hall is at 7904 35th Avenue SW in West Seattle 98126. Call (206) 937-3613 or email kenyon@kenyonhall.org and check kenyonhall.org for the calendar.

title: Inside
venue_description:
Inside

Inside is a healing arts studio and event space in downtown Seattle. It offers yoga and sound baths and creative sessions and it describes itself as a sanctuary that uses the arts to support wellness and personal growth.

Open Mic Night

On the second Saturday of every month Inside hosts an Open Mic Night at 7:30 PM. Poets and singers and musicians and storytellers and dancers are all welcome. Each act gets up to 5 minutes and sign-up happens at the venue on the day of the event. Tickets are $5 in advance and $7 at the door. Deaunte Damper hosts and the room provides a sound system with two microphones and a spotlight.

Atmosphere

The studio feels calm and intimate and the audience is supportive. It is a great space for soulful singers and acoustic players and first-time performers.

Good to Know

Inside is at 1313 Fourth Avenue in downtown Seattle 98101. The open mic is 21 and over. Visit aspaceinside.com for details.
